summary.prose: This Story puts every chat message for a repository into one shared queue and runs them one at a time, in order, whichever chat or window they come from. A message sent while a turn runs no longer hides or interrupts it: it waits and runs when the turn ends. The queue is a small SQLite file per repository that all windows share; the window that owns the message at the front takes the repository's lease, marks the message taken and runs it with the chat's existing turn engine.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A shared per-repository SQLite queue (node:sqlite, WAL, busy timeout) under ~/.insrc, written only in short IMMEDIATE transactions, with three tables: messages in queue order, a single-row repo lease with a heartbeat, and window presence keyed by a window key that survives a reload. A deps-injected queue worker in each window decides from the database alone when to take the lease, acknowledges the head message (queued -> processing) in the same transaction, and hands the turn to the existing turn lifecycle with its newest-wins rule removed; the per-session lease stays underneath as a guard against two CLI processes on one session. Takeover, not-delivered marking, retries and the flush are rules over these tables, and the outbox is a projection of them posted to the chat webview.

ownedContracts.name: ChatQueueStore
ownedContracts.purpose: The per-repository store and every transaction on it: enqueue with the bound check, the acknowledgement, state changes, cancel and dismiss, resend, the flush, and reading the queue for a view.

ownedContracts.name: RepoLease and WindowPresence
ownedContracts.purpose: Which window runs the repository's turn now, with the CLI process that turn started, and which windows are alive, so a dead window is told from a slow or reloading one and a CLI that outlived its window keeps the repository.

ownedContracts.name: TurnOutcome
ownedContracts.purpose: What the turn runner reports to the worker when a queued turn and its continuations end, including a turn whose view was detached, so the worker can finish, fail or retry the message and release the lease only when no CLI of that turn is still running.

ownedContracts.name: ChatQueueWorker
ownedContracts.purpose: The per-window loop that watches the store, keeps presence and the lease fresh, decides what runs next and asks the chat host to run it; and the enqueue entry point every sender uses.

boundary.internal: The SQLite schema, its migrations and pragmas (WAL, busy_timeout), the repo key and the store's file location, the window key kept in workspace storage, the worker's polling cadence and timers, and the chat host's change from starting turns to submitting them. Every caller of runTurn is accounted for: the webview's submit-turn and the attachment submit enqueue a 'typed' message; the approval grant's re-run (chat-panel.ts:578, with allowedTools and suppressEcho) and the selection continuation (:1671, suppressEcho) are continuations of the turn already holding the lease and run under it, off the queue; submitExternal enqueues a 'review-pane' message (s5). The runner opens the panel and shows the message's chat when needed, and reports the lease's CLI process at spawn. turn-lifecycle.ts gains onSpawn with an exit promise that survives detach(), for live and followed turns (the tests that pin newest-wins or the supersede change: turn-lifecycle.test.ts:205 'a second start drops a turn still waiting for its lease', :229, :252, :728, :766, :984; chat-panel.test.ts:138 'single-in-flight: a second submit supersedes the first', :1318 (its 'a newer turn's start' leg: a submit no longer ends the running turn's diff state, since runTurn's start no longer calls endDiffTurn for a queued message), :2854 'Stop ends the running process at once and cancels a waiting message' (now: the waiting message runs after Stop), :4745, :5018, and the presenter tests of a superseded turn at :5302 and :5455 (now: there are no superseded turns); the rest stand). Sending a message never touches the running turn: submit and enqueue no longer call supersedeQueuedApprovals (chat-panel.ts:1432 and :1506, and drainExternal's call at :702 goes with the list in s5), so a typed message waits behind a waiting card, which the user answers; chat-panel.test.ts:4745 changes to assert the card stays. A waiting approval or selection card of the running turn ends at an answer, Stop, a chat switch, the panel closing or CONTINUATION_WAIT_MS; the message then finishes 'stopped', which leaves it failed with a resend, and the lease is released. A head message whose session no longer exists fails with that reason. Mixed plugin versions: a window still running the previous plugin after an update starts turns outside the queue until it is reloaded; VS Code asks for that reload after an extension update, the store records the plugin version that created it, and s1's hand check covers reloading every window. The plugin's test runtime is pinned to a Node with unflagged node:sqlite (engines.node >= 22.13). The newest-wins supersede in turn-lifecycle.ts is removed; a chat switch, the panel closing or adopt() detach the view only, and the runner then resolves 'detached-ended' when the detached CLI exits, the window holding and heartbeating the lease until then; a pipe turn, which detach() stops (turn-lifecycle.ts:517-525), resolves 'stopped' and so stays as a failed message with a resend. Stop ends the running turn and releases the lease. The minimum VS Code version and the plain 'unsupported VS Code' message when node:sqlite cannot load are part of s1.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The outbox's markup, styles (VS Code theme variables, the chat panel's rounded style) and its live updates in the webview, the projection from queue rows to OutboxView for the shown session (processing rows are dropped: the running message is in the transcript), and the handling of the four outbox actions in the chat host. When the queue is held by a waiting approval or selection card, other chats' outboxes say which chat it is waiting on (blockedBy).

The takeover rule (lease stale for LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS and both the holder window's process and the lease's CLI process gone), marking a processing message failed when its window died with no CLI left, re-attaching a turn whose CLI survived a reload (the reloaded window, same window key, reclaims the lease with reclaim() and follows the turn through the session's saved cursor), the not-delivered rule for a head message whose window is closed (no live presence past PRESENCE_GRACE_MS and its process gone), and the flush that keeps the stored records within QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND.

The classification of a failed turn's error into an InfraCause, the 'acted' tracking from the turn's tool-call, file-edit and tool-result events, the retry schedule (10 s, 1 min, 5 min; at most 3), the retrying state's row in the outbox with its countdown, retry-now and cancel, and the authentication message.

A pane decision goes to the chat the review pane hands over to today: the chat shown in this window's panel, or, when the panel is closed, the chat the panel opens on (this window's last active chat). It is submitted through ChatQueueWorker.submit with origin 'review-pane', and the panel is opened. submitExternal returns ExternalSubmitResult = 'queued' | { readonly kind: 'unavailable'; readonly note: string } (from EnqueueResult: ok -> 'queued', full / busy / unavailable -> unavailable with the queue's note; 'sent' is no longer returned since every message queues), and the review host's notifyChat type, ChatHandOver and decisionResultLine carry the note so the pane shows why a decision was refused; the change sites are ExternalSubmitResult in chat-panel.ts:148-154, the review host's notifyChat dep type and ChatHandOver in docs-review-panel.ts:45 and :65 with the hand-over sentence at :2452 (the 'sent' branch goes; 'queued' reads 'Sent to the chat; it waits its turn in the outbox.'; 'unavailable' shows the queue's note), the binding in extension.ts:712, and the tests review-wiring.test.ts, docs-review-decision.test.ts (its default notifyChat returning 'sent' at :126 and the result lines at :457-462) and chat-panel.test.ts's submitExternal suite (:4931-5235), which assert 'sent', the wording and the drain order. The waitingExternal list and drainExternal are removed. Attachments: liveSessionIds() across every repository's queue file under ~/.insrc/chat-queue is added to the start-up sweep's keep set (which takes session ids, extension.ts:470, attachment-store.ts:199), and session eviction skips any session with live rows in any queue: createFileChatSessionStore (session-file-store.ts: FileStoreDeps at :98-105, evictBeyondCap at :285-313, built at extension.ts:459) gains a keep predicate dependency: the oldest-first eviction skips kept sessions and evicts other sessions instead to respect the cap, since onEvict runs after the eviction and cannot veto it.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — the shared queue and in-order turns

nonFunctional.performance: Enqueue, acknowledge and finish are each one IMMEDIATE transaction of a few rows, under 10 ms on a local disk; a window polls data_version every 500 ms while its repository has live rows or it holds the lease, and every 5 s otherwise; a waiting message starts within about one poll interval of the turn ahead of it ending.
nonFunctional.security: The store holds message text and attachment paths in the user's home directory with the same permissions as the chat sessions under ~/.insrc; no new network surface; no credentials are stored.
nonFunctional.observability: Every acknowledgement, takeover, not-delivered marking, retry and refusal is logged through the chat's logger with the message key and window key; the outbox shows each message's state and error to the user.
nonFunctional.durability: WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL; a crashed window leaves at most an uncommitted transaction, which SQLite rolls back; done rows are deleted at once and the store never holds more than QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND live rows. The store records the plugin version that created it and its schema version; a newer schema is migrated in one transaction on open.

api.name: ChatQueueStore
api.signature: createChatQueueStore(deps: { readonly path: string; readonly openDatabase: (path: string) => SqliteDatabase; readonly now: () => number; readonly pluginVersion: string; readonly log: ChatPanelLogger }): ChatQueueStore & ChatQueueLeases

parameters.name: deps.path
parameters.purpose: The repository's database file, ~/.insrc/chat-queue/<repo key>.sqlite; its directory is created if missing.

parameters.name: deps.openDatabase
parameters.purpose: Opens the file with node:sqlite's DatabaseSync; injected so the module stays free of the runtime check and tests can use a temp file. SqliteDatabase is the subset used: exec, prepare(...).run/get/all.

parameters.name: deps.pluginVersion
parameters.purpose: Recorded in the meta table when the store is created.

returns.meaning: New module chat-queue-store.ts implementing HLD sc1 and sc2. On open: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout=5000; schema version 1 created or migrated in one transaction (tables messages, lease, presence, meta). Every write is BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT. enqueue counts live rows and returns { ok:false, reason:'full', note } at QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND (500), else inserts with state queued and the next seq. head() returns the first row in seq order whose state is queued or retrying. acknowledge(seq, claim) succeeds only when the row is that head, its state is queued (or retrying and due) and the lease row is empty: it sets the lease { windowKey, pid, pidStartedAt, seq, heartbeatAt: now } and the row's state to processing in the same transaction. finish(seq, outcome) maps done and detached-ended to DELETE, stopped to failed with error 'stopped by the user' (or the given reason), failed to failed with its error (s4 adds retrying), not-delivered to not-delivered (s3), and clears the lease when it names seq. cancel deletes a queued or retrying row; dismiss deletes a failed or not-delivered row; resend inserts a copy at the back with a new turn id and deletes the old row. attachCli, heartbeat, release, presence and windowAlive operate on the lease and presence rows; takeOver and reclaim are declared here and return false until s3 implements their rules. dataVersion() reads PRAGMA data_version.

errors.condition: SQLITE_BUSY persisting past busy_timeout: the caller gets a note, nothing is lost.
openDatabase throws (node:sqlite missing) or the schema version is newer than this plugin knows; extension.ts turns it into the 'unsupported' notice.

preconditions: One store per repository file per window; two windows open the same file
postconditions: A message is acknowledged at most once, by one window
Rows run in seq order; a retrying head is never skipped
done rows never remain; live rows never exceed 500

api.name: ChatQueueWorker

parameters.name: deps.claim
parameters.purpose: This window: its window key (stable across reloads) and extension-host pid with start time.

parameters.name: deps.isAlive
parameters.purpose: Process check built in extension.ts from session-lock.ts's defaultIsAlive(pid) and defaultProcessStartTime(pid) (the pid is alive and, when a start time is given, it matches).

returns.meaning: New module chat-queue-worker.ts implementing HLD sc4. It refreshes this window's presence every LEASE_HEARTBEAT_MS; polls store.dataVersion() every 500 ms while the store has live rows or this window holds the lease, every 5 s otherwise; on a change it emits onChange(list()). Because PRAGMA data_version does not change for a connection's own commits, the store also counts its own committed writes (a local version bumped by every enqueue, acknowledge, finish, cancel, dismiss, resend, attachCli and release); the worker compares both, so onChange fires after this window's writes too, as sc4 requires. When idle (not running) and head() is this window's (windowKey === claim.windowKey) and not a retrying row still waiting, it calls acknowledge(head.seq, claim); on success it starts heartbeating the lease every LEASE_HEARTBEAT_MS, calls runner.run(message, onSpawn) where onSpawn calls attachCli, and on the outcome calls finish(seq, outcome) and release(claim); if either throws (SQLITE_BUSY past the timeout), the pair is kept as a pending finish and retried on every poll until it commits, and the worker takes no new message meanwhile. One message runs at a time per window, and the lease makes that one per repository. submit() enqueues and triggers an immediate check. liveSessionIds() lists sessions with live rows. dispose() stops the timers, removes this window's presence row, and releases a held lease when the turn's CLI has already exited (finishing its message as the runner reported, or as failed 'the window closed during the turn'); a lease whose CLI is still running is left to its heartbeat timeout, which s3's takeover acts on.

errors.condition: A runner that rejects is treated as failed with the error and acted=true (so it is never retried); store errors are logged and retried on the next poll.

postconditions: A window never runs two messages at once
A head message of another window is left to that window

api.name: QueuedTurnRunner
api.signature: interface QueuedTurnRunner { run(message: QueuedMessage, onSpawn: (cli: { readonly pid?: number | undefined; readonly startedAt?: number | undefined }) => void): Promise<TurnOutcome> }

parameters.name: message
parameters.purpose: The acknowledged message: its session, text and attachments (AttachmentRef as the attachment store gives it).

parameters.name: onSpawn
parameters.purpose: Called once the turn's CLI is spawned, so the lease records the CLI process.

returns.meaning: Implemented by createChatPanelHost as runQueued. It opens the panel if it is closed and shows the message's session if another is shown (posting a note 'Running your queued message in <title>'); if the session no longer exists it resolves failed 'the chat no longer exists'. It posts 'turn-running' { sessionId } to the webview, which sets its running state (setRunning(true) and the progress line, as doSubmit does today) so the send button becomes Stop for a queued turn that started without a click (a message typed mid-turn, one from another window or after a reload); the turn's done or error clears it as today. It then runs what startTurn does today for that session (user row and live echo, first-message title, save, TurnRequest with readDirs, turns.start) and resolves when the turn and its continuations have ended; it also resolves when turns.start()'s promise settles with no terminal event, no reported error and no onSpawn call (the turn was dropped while waiting for the session lease or in beforeRun, e.g. a chat switch at that moment): stopped with error 'the turn was dropped before it started'. Otherwise: done on a terminal done; failed with the error (acted=true until s4 tracks it) on a terminal error or a reported error; stopped on Stop: cancel-turn (chat-panel.ts:1509-1514) sets a stop flag on the running queued message, and that flag takes precedence over the terminal error a stopped CLI produces ('the CLI ended without finishing the turn'), so a Stop is always 'stopped by the user', never a failure that s4 could retry; detached-ended when the view was detached and the detached CLI's exited promise settles (a pipe turn, which detach() stops, resolves stopped). A continuation (the approval grant's re-run and the selection continuation, which call runTurn with allowedTools or suppressEcho) runs under the same lease, off the queue, and the message resolves only after the last continuation ends; a waiting approval or selection card ends at an answer, Stop, a chat switch, the panel closing or CONTINUATION_WAIT_MS (10 minutes), and then the message resolves stopped with error 'no answer to the approval'.

preconditions: The worker acknowledged the message for this window
postconditions: The user row is pushed to the transcript only when the message runs (it leaves the outbox for the transcript)

api.name: createTurnLifecycle
api.signature: createTurnLifecycle(deps: TurnLifecycleDeps): TurnLifecycle  // TurnSink and FollowSink gain onSpawn?(cli: { pid?: number; startedAt?: number; exited: Promise<void> }): void

returns.meaning: Two changes, as the HLD decides. (1) The newest-wins supersede is removed: start() no longer aborts a turn waiting for the session lease and no longer takes over reporting from a turn in progress; a start() made while a turn of this lifecycle is in progress waits until that turn has ended (start calls are chained) and only then takes its generation, so the earlier turn is never dropped. The generation still guards detach(), invalidate() and Stop, and a start still waiting in the chain is dropped by them too: stop(), detach() and invalidate() bump a chain epoch that the chained start checks when it resumes, so it never spawns (the grant re-run chained inside onTerminal cannot run after its message resolved stopped). The tests that pinned the supersede change as the HLD lists (turn-lifecycle.test.ts:205, :229, :252, :728, :766, :984: a second start now runs after the first). (2) Both sinks gain onSpawn, called from the existing onSpawn closure of run() and from follow()'s resumed process, with an exited promise that settles on the process's exit and survives detach(). onSpawn is called for every spawned process, also one without a pid (TurnProcess.pid is number | undefined, cli-adapter.ts:74): the pid is then absent, the lease records no CLI, and 'spawned' is still known, so runQueued never mistakes it for a turn dropped before it started.

errors.condition: onSpawn throwing is logged and ignored.

postconditions: A detached session-file turn's CLI exit is observable to the chat host
A second start() runs after the first ends; no turn is dropped by a later start
A start waiting in the chain is dropped by stop(), detach() and invalidate() and never spawns

api.name: createChatPanelHost
api.signature: createChatPanelHost(deps: ChatPanelHostDeps & { readonly queue?: ((runner: QueuedTurnRunner) => ChatQueueWorker) | undefined }): ChatPanelHost

parameters.name: deps.queue
parameters.purpose: Builds the window's worker over the repository's store with the host's runner; absent (tests, or node:sqlite unavailable) keeps today's direct start path.

returns.meaning: With a queue: the webview's submit-turn and the attachment submit call worker.submit({ sessionId, text, origin: 'typed', attachments }) instead of runTurn, and no longer call supersedeQueuedApprovals (chat-panel.ts:1432, :1506), so sending never touches the running turn; a refused submit posts the queue's note as a chat notice. The grant re-run (:578) and the selection continuation (:1671) keep calling runTurn directly, as continuations under the lease. Stop calls turns.stop(); the running message then resolves stopped. The host exposes the runner. submitExternal and drainExternal are left to s5, which moves them onto the queue; until then drainExternal (chat-panel.ts:697-704) is a third direct start, and in s1 it is held back while this window's worker is running a message (it waits for the worker to be idle). A pane decision in Phase A can still start a turn while another window's queued turn holds the lease: a stated rollout gap closed by s5.

errors.condition: A submit refused by the queue is shown, never thrown.

postconditions: A typed message never starts a turn directly while a queue is present

api.name: activate (extension.ts)

parameters.name: context
parameters.purpose: Gives workspaceState for the window key.

returns.meaning: Builds the queue for the chat: the window key is read from workspaceState 'insrc.chat.windowKey' (a random id created once); the repo key is the sha256 (first 16 hex) of the real path of `git -C <chat folder> rev-parse --show-toplevel`, else the real path of the folder, else of process.cwd(); the store opens at ~/.insrc/chat-queue/<repo key>.sqlite through openDatabase = (p) => new (require('node:sqlite').DatabaseSync)(p). As DEF k5 requires, package.json engines.vscode rises to ^1.141.0, the version whose runtime was checked (Electron 43, Node 24.21), so an older VS Code does not install this plugin version. If opening the store still throws (a runtime without the module, e.g. a modified build), the chat runs without the queue (today's behaviour) and says plainly once: 'This VS Code is not supported by the chat queue: its runtime cannot load node:sqlite. Messages run as before.' The extension also gives the worker isAlive = (pid, startedAt) => defaultIsAlive(pid) && (startedAt === undefined || defaultProcessStartTime(pid) === startedAt), built from session-lock.ts's two existing checks. The plugin's tests need Node >= 22.13 (node:sqlite unflagged); the repo's toolchain runs Node 22.22 and 24.

errorCases.scenario: A queued turn is dropped before it starts (a chat switch or panel close while it waits for the session lease or runs beforeRun)

errorCases.scenario: finish or release fails after a turn ends (SQLITE_BUSY past the timeout)

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test run with tsx (npx tsx --test) under Node >= 22.13 so node:sqlite is unflagged (the repo's toolchain runs Node 22.22 and 24); the two-process test forks a child with child_process.fork over a temp database file; the chat host tests use the existing fake channel and gated adapters

migration.stateBefore: A typed message starts a turn at once and the newest message wins: the running turn stops reporting and the new one waits for the session's previous CLI to exit. Turns of different chats run at the same time.
migration.stateAfter: Every typed message goes into the repository's shared queue and runs in order, one turn per repository; the running turn keeps reporting; Stop leaves the message failed with a resend.

migrationSteps.action: Add chat-queue-store.ts with the schema and transactions, and its tests including the two-process test
Remove the newest-wins supersede from the turn lifecycle (chained starts) and add onSpawn with the exit promise to its sinks; update the lifecycle tests the HLD lists
Give the chat host the runner and route typed messages through the queue; update the chat-panel tests the HLD lists
Wire the repo key, window key and store in extension.ts with the fallback and notice; raise engines.vscode to ^1.141.0 and add engines.node >=22.13
Run the suite, build, package, install; hand check with two windows

migration.backwardCompat: A new file per repository under ~/.insrc/chat-queue; nothing existing is rewritten. Without node:sqlite the chat keeps today's direct path. A window still on the old plugin starts turns outside the queue until reloaded. Phase A gaps closed by later Stories: a lease held by a crashed window, or by a window closed while its CLI still runs, waits for s3's takeover; a closed window's message at the head waits for s3's not-delivered rule; and a review-pane decision can start a turn outside the queue until s5.

alternativesConsidered.name: Store and worker as two new modules; the chat host submits and supplies the runner
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: chat-queue-store.ts and chat-queue-worker.ts as the HLD lays out; the chat host's typed and pane messages call worker.submit, and the host's runQueued is the QueuedTurnRunner
alternativesConsidered.approach: chat-queue-store.ts wraps one node:sqlite database (opened through an injected factory) with the schema, pragmas and every transaction of sc1 and sc2. chat-queue-worker.ts owns timing: presence and lease heartbeats, data_version polling, deciding to acknowledge the head, and calling the runner. The chat host keeps the turn path it has: runQueued(message) shows the message's chat, then does what startTurn does today (transcript row, echo, title, request) and resolves a TurnOutcome from the sink.
pros: Matches the HLD's contracts one to one
The store is testable on its own against a temp file, also from two processes
The chat host's turn path (diff sections, approvals, presenter) is reused unchanged
cons: The chat host grows a runner and loses its direct start path, a broad change to a 1800-line file

alternativesConsidered.name: One combined queue module
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Store and worker in one file with one factory
alternativesConsidered.approach: A single chat-queue.ts holds the schema, transactions, timers and the run decision behind one factory.
cons: Timers and SQL mixed: the store cannot be tested from two processes without the timers
Diverges from the HLD's sc1/sc4 split that s3 and s4 consume
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Harder to test the cross-process guarantees.

alternativesConsidered.name: Queue inside the turn lifecycle
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: turn-lifecycle.ts itself enqueues and decides when to run
alternativesConsidered.approach: turns.start would enqueue and run when its message reaches the front, so the chat host would not change.
pros: Smallest change to the chat host
cons: The lifecycle is per window and per session; the repo-wide queue, presence and other chats' messages do not belong there
Mixes the engine of one turn with scheduling across windows, against the HLD's boundary
